newsitem.title: UK: Dollar drifts lower in subdued European trade.
newsitem.headline: Dollar drifts lower in subdued European trade.

text.p: The dollar was drifting lower against the mark and the yen in late European trade but was keeping well within its recent ranges.

In late afternoon trade, the dollar was testing its session lows against the mark, trading just above 1.4750 marks. Against the yen, it was slipping away from its earlier highs but remained steady above 108 yen.

"There were some good corporate offers in dollar/mark above 1.48 this morning which started the dollar's drift downwards throughout the day," said a British bank dealer. "But there's no real conviction, it's still a very rangebound market."
The dollar spiked up overnight on the weaker than expected quarterly Tankan report in Japan, lifting it above 108 yen and eventually to a session high in Europe of 108.50.
The Tankan's diffusion index for major manufacturers fell to minus seven from minus three in the previous report.

Japanese Finance Minister Waturo Kubo said he believed the Bank of Japan's interest rate policy, which has been geared towards spurring sluggish economic growth, had not changed after the quarterly survey.
Dealers said the soft Tankan was pressuring the yen as pre-report concern over higher near-term rates in Japan eased.
By 1529 GMT, the dollar was trading at 108.42/52 yen and 1.4761/65 marks against 107.75/85 and 1.4791/94 late Tuesday.
The yen was also weaker against the mark which pushed up through key resistance at 73.30 in Europe to 73.48/50 yen, its European session high. It stood at 72.85/86 on Tuesday.
Sterling was pushing higher against the dollar, twice challenging key psychological resistance at $1.56 before settling back to $1.5589/97 at 1537 GMT.
"People are beginning to watch cable now that it's up to this big resistance area at $1.56. If it can break through here then we could see some big gains," said the UK bank dealer.
Earlier today, the UK's July non-EU trade deficit narrowed to 506 million stg against a forecast shortfall of around 900 million. The UK's global trade deficit June was 1.12 billion.
Dealers said the data lent some support to the pound but was not considered a major factor in its performance today.
Sterling was firmer against the mark, moving above 2.30 marks to 2.3019/30 by 1548 GMT.

On the crosses, the mark was still firm but edging off the day's highs by late afternoon. However, EMU concerns and the forthcoming round of European budget talks were likely to keep it underpinned for now. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 6745
